Targets breeding/slaughtering/distributing/selling DOGS SPECIFICALLY for meat consumption - not a general animal-cruelty provision, hence single_species_targeted rather than a general animal_scope value. Covers purposely crushing, burning, drowning, suffocating, impaling, or otherwise inflicting serious bodily injury on a 'living non-human mammal, bird, reptile, or amphibian' - fish and invertebrates explicitly absent from the definition. Originally enacted 1999 targeting only 'crush videos' (depictions); the PACT Act 2019 expanded it to criminalize the underlying CONDUCT itself - the single most significant federal expansion in the 2015-2026 window. The commonly-cited '$250,000' fine figure likely derives from the GENERAL federal felony fine schedule (18 U.S.C. S3571) rather than being S48-specific - left blank here as unconfirmed rather than asserted. NO GENERAL FEDERAL CRUELTY OFFENCE EXISTS beyond this narrow, commerce-tied provision - general cruelty/neglect/abandonment/killing is exclusively STATE law in the US (see ALDF's 50-state rankings, referenced in PRD SS7, for that layer).

7 U.S.C. S2132(g): dog, cat, nonhuman primate, guinea pig, hamster, rabbit, or other warm-blooded animal the Secretary designates - EXPLICITLY EXCLUDING birds, rats/mice bred for research, horses not used in research, and farm animals used for food/fiber. Applies only to USDA-licensed dealers/exhibitors/research facilities - imposes husbandry/care standards enforced via CIVIL penalties and license actions (APHIS), not a criminal cruelty offence for private owners. Enforcement reportedly weakened post-SEC v. Jarkesy (June 2024 Supreme Court ruling restricting in-house civil-penalty adjudication) - advocacy-sourced reporting (not government-confirmed) cites only 5 fines issued in the following 14 months, and a 2025 USDA OIG audit finding 80% of reviewed dog breeders had at least one noncompliance.

aggravating_factors: Second or subsequent offence: prohibition order MINIMUM 5 years (vs. discretionary duration for a first offence).
notes: s.445.1(1)(a): wilfully causing/permitting unnecessary pain, suffering, or injury to ANY 'animal or bird' - no vertebrate or domestic-status qualifier stated in the fetched text, unlike most other jurisdictions researched. s.447: building/maintaining an arena for animal fighting. Subsection (3) repealed by 2019, c.17, s.3 (Bill C-84).

aggravating_factors: Pre-2021-06-29 maximum was 6 months (summary-only, no indictable tier existed). Sentencing Act 2021 raised the indictable maximum to 5 years with an UNLIMITED fine (no numeric cap - left blank here rather than asserting a false ceiling).
notes: s.4 (unnecessary suffering): act/omission causing suffering, defendant knew or ought to have known, suffering unnecessary (courts weigh avoidability, legality, legitimate purpose, proportionality, reasonable-competent-person standard); carve-out for 'relevant officers' (police) reasonably using an animal in duty. 'Protected animal' scope (vertebrates domesticated in the British Islands, under human control, or not living in a wild state) not independently verified word-for-word this round. s.9 (duty of care): proactive failure to take reasonable steps to meet the animal's needs 'to the extent required by good practice', via the five welfare needs (suitable environment; suitable diet; ability to exhibit normal behaviour; appropriate housing with/apart from other animals; protection from pain/suffering/injury/disease). PENALTY FIELDS LEFT BLANK DELIBERATELY: the verified post-2021 5-year/unlimited-fine tier was confirmed for ss.4,5,6(1)-(2),7,8 specifically - s.9 was NOT confirmed to be part of that same list in this round's research. aggravating_factors: Art.25-1: causing multiple animal deaths via drugs/firearms in serious cases raises the penalty to 1-5yr + fine NT$500,000-5,000,000.

Art.3 defines 'animal' as dogs, cats, and other vertebrates reared/kept by humans, expressly including livestock, laboratory/experimental animals, and pets - wild animals in their natural habitat fall under the separate Wildlife Conservation Act. Separately, dog/cat meat sale/consumption/possession carries an ADMINISTRATIVE fine NT$50,000-250,000 with mandatory name-and-shame disclosure (a consumption ban, not modeled as its own cruelty-provision row). Corporate/organizational liability not confirmed this round.

Art.27-1: up to 1 year imprisonment/detention or fine up to NT$30,000 for spreading cruelty depictions, exempting academic/public-interest use. Added by the 2010-01-27 amendment - NOT a 2022 addition as sometimes assumed.

Scope per a snippet-level source: 'any mammal, bird, reptile, amphibian, fish or any other vertebrate or invertebrate whether wild or tame' - an explicit exhaustive-sounding list covering essentially everything, distinct from Canada's silence-based undifferentiated scope. IMPORTANT: this HK$200,000/3-year maximum was NOT set by a 2023/2024 amendment (a claim that circulates but is confirmed false) - it dates to the 2006 amendment. As of Feb 2026 (LCQ15), a reform package (duty-of-care offence, indictable tier, disqualification orders, higher penalties) has been under consultation since 2019/May 2022 but remains UNENACTED. Summary offence only (magistrates' courts), 6-month prosecution time-bar from offence date - a 2021 HKU study found >20% of offenders evade prosecution via the time-bar, only ~50% of convicted abusers jailed, mostly <=6 weeks. No evidence of a filming/distribution offence found this round (gap, not confirmed absence). SPCA HK has NO delegated statutory enforcement power despite handling 20,000+ calls/year - AFCD and Police jointly enforce; over 90% of AFCD-received reports are non-cruelty nuisance complaints; 82 prosecutions (HKPF+AFCD combined) 2023-2025.

Article 44: killing/injuring a protected animal (愛護動物) without justifiable cause. Raised from 2yr/JPY2M under the 2012 law to the current 5yr/JPY5M via the 2019 reform, staged effective June 2022/2023/2024 (correcting the more commonly assumed 2020-2022 staging - effective_date recorded here is the FINAL stage). Protected-animal list: cattle, horses, pigs, sheep, goats, dogs, cats, domestic rabbits, chickens, domestic pigeons, domestic ducks, plus any other mammal/bird/reptile 'in human possession' - excludes fish, amphibians, invertebrates, AND feral/wild populations of the same species. NPA-recorded arrests/cleared cases under Art.44: 2015=56, 2016=62, 2017=68, 2018=84, 2019=105, 2020=102, 2021=170, 2022=166, 2023=181 (record high), 2024=160 (down 11.6% from the record but still historically high).

Article 44: cruelty/neglect (虐待 - withholding food/water, confinement causing debilitation, failure to treat sick/injured animals, hoarding in filth) and abandonment (遺棄), each up to 1yr/JPY1M. Abandonment was previously FINE-ONLY (max JPY500,000, no custodial penalty) before this reform. Organizing animal fighting (dogfighting) has NO national prohibition - only patchwork prefectural ordinances (Tokyo/Kanagawa/Fukui/Ishikawa ban it; Hokkaido licenses it for the Tosa breed). Filming/distributing cruelty content has no dedicated offense - the NPA treats cruelty publicized on video-sharing sites as an Article 44 enforcement priority, not a separate crime.

The houdverbod (ownership ban) became a STANDALONE measure from 2024-01-01, up to 30 years or life for serious/repeat cases - a notably severe outlier vs. other jurisdictions' typical 5-year caps; violating it is itself an offence (1wk per animal, up to 2-5wks for multiple). aggravating_factors: Corporate/body-corporate tier: fine up to NZD 500,000. [SNIPPET-LEVEL, current figures NOT independently verified against primary text this round - see notes for the verified-but-superseded 2007 baseline.]
notes: UPGRADED 2026-09-15: a real primary-source PDF was recovered (Parliamentary Counsel Office reprint, 'as at 2007-09-03', hosted by University of Auckland's Liggins Institute) after ~10 prior fetch attempts against legislation.govt.nz/nzlii.org all failed - confirmed this round to be a Cloudflare JS-challenge wall, not a URL problem. s.2 (VERIFIED, verbatim): 'Animal' = any live member of the animal kingdom that is a mammal, bird, reptile, amphibian, or fish (bony or cartilaginous), OR any octopus, squid, crab, lobster, or crayfish (including freshwater crayfish), or any other species declared by Order in Council; includes mammalian foetuses/avian-reptilian pre-hatched young in the last half of gestation and marsupial pouch young; excludes human beings. This names cephalopods AND decapod crustaceans directly in the statute's primary definition (not via delegated regulation, contrast Switzerland) - hence the new animal_scope value. There is NO section 3A - the 2015 sentience recognition was inserted into the Act's LONG TITLE (statement of purpose) by the Animal Welfare Amendment Act (No 2) 2015, not as an operative numbered section - this is a policy-framing statement, not an independently enforceable provision, an important distinction for cross-jurisdictional comparison. PENALTY HISTORY: 2007-verified baseline (this Act as originally enacted): s.28 (wilful ill-treatment causing permanent disability/death/necessary destruction), on indictment - individual up to 3 years/NZD 50,000, body corporate up to NZD 250,000. This was raised to the current 5-year/NZD 100,000 figure (recorded in this row) via a later amendment; a new s.28A 'Reckless ill-treatment of animals' was inserted 2010-07-07 by the Animal Welfare Amendment Act 2010 (NOT 2015 as this database's prior placeholder speculated) mirroring s.28's threshold. The current dollar figures rest on snippet-level secondary-source corroboration, not a primary-text refetch of the current consolidated version - flag accordingly. No dedicated filming/distribution offence exists in this Act; cruelty content depicting animals MAY fall under the separate Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993's general 'objectionable material' regime (trading up to 14yr, possession up to 10yr/NZD 50,000) - but no confirmed instance of this being applied to an animal-cruelty case was found; this is inference from statutory scope, not a confirmed application, and is not modeled as its own provision row.

aggravating_factors: Fine tiers: 20,000-100,000 patacas (serious infractions); 4,000-20,000 (intermediate); 2,000-10,000 (minor); flat 2,000 (minimal infractions) - four distinct tiers by severity, verified via direct fetch, though the exact tier-definition boundaries were not verbatim-quoted (structured extract, snippet-level for the boundary criteria specifically, verified for the amounts themselves).
notes: Art.29: the ADMINISTRATIVE-infraction counterpart to Art.25's criminal tier (MO-L42016-P1) - covers cruelty not reaching the criminal threshold (no grave injury/mutilation/organ loss/death, or no proven intent). Accessory sanctions: confiscation of the animal, a 1-3 year ownership ban, activity restriction, or establishment closure.

aggravating_factors: Body-corporate tier: fine up to NZD 125,000. [2007-VERIFIED baseline - whether this specific tier's figures have since been raised is UNCONFIRMED this round; do not assume it moved in step with s.28's increase.]
notes: s.25 (VERIFIED, 2007 text): general offences covering breaches of ss.12/14/21/22/23 (the owner/person-in-charge duty to meet an animal's physical, health, and behavioural needs). This is the lower, duty-of-care tier, distinct from s.28's wilful/reckless ill-treatment tier (see NZ-AWA1999-P1).
